fix: Only the schema, the workspace, the log-like tables and the rows of workspace.db (connections and their tests) carry UUIDv7 ids

what: ids increase "by the file's one writer", but t05 only makes each id greater than the last the PROCESS issued: a new process whose clock is behind the file's greatest id issues smaller ids, and the integrity queries operation-after-its-turn / turn-takes-back-an-earlier-turn then refuse the commit
evidence: t05 reads crates: uuid ContextV7 "greater than the last the process issued"
fix: t05: on opening a file, the generator starts after the greatest UUIDv7 the file holds

what: it never creates, alters or drops a table — yet the store (t05) creates every table; the exception is only in the breach
fix: text: "no code creates, alters or drops a table, a column, an index or a constraint but the store, from these files alone"

what: breach says the store's tests plant a row breaking "each constraint and each integrity query"; t05 has one item for one FK, one check, one integrity query — 11 cortex queries + 6 MySQL + 1 Quill go untested
fix: t05: one data-driven item — every integrity query of every owner refuses the commit given the violating row its fixtures name (crates/store/tests/fixtures/violations), and a query with no fixture fails the test

what: claims shared code naming "an engine table or an engine column" is caught: the architecture check on main catches an engine id inside an identifier (so mysql__… is caught) but no engine column name (row_format, charset)
fix: add the vocabulary guard (finding 12) and name it here

what: the architecture check is said to catch an engine's connection field, kind, option, table or column in shared code; on main it checks database names only (the vocabulary check was in held #91, a not_source). Shared code arrives in t05 (the store) with nothing guarding it
fix: t03 (which builds the test registry) also extends tools/architecture: every engine's field keys, kind ids, option keys, table and column names, read from what each declares, refused in shared code as a string literal or a member

what: the build session's settings, which deny the tools that spawn or message another agent / "(attribution off)": no such settings are named anywhere for SchemaForge builds
evidence: no settings file in the repository (by the operator's choice); the operator keeps a build configuration outside it

what: a test outside the tests element's items (the_repository_passes_the_spec_check); root method tests: "one test per item and none outside the list"
fix: make it an item of the tests element (tests path tools/specs/tests/, both files)

what: no guard that every table's primary key is one column named id, TEXT — which t02 (a Row's id column) and value/row_changes.row_id rely on
fix: step 8: every table has exactly one primary key, the column id, of type TEXT

what: a foreign key whose target columns are not the target table's primary key (or a unique key) loads fine and fails only at the first insert ("foreign key mismatch"); the check would pass it
fix: step 9: every foreign key's target columns are its target table's primary key

what: a column definition (an identifier, quoted or not, then a type): the types are not named, so whether e.g. a constraint line counts is the agent's reading
evidence: schema files use TEXT, INTEGER, ANY
fix: name them: TEXT, INTEGER, REAL, BLOB or ANY

what: specs/lessons.xml is in specs/ but the check reads root, rules and tasks only: a broken lessons.xml passes
fix: step 1: specs/lessons.xml too, parsed, its root lessons with product, version, date, each lesson with id, date, found, seen, does

what: a sequence task's depends naming no task id is not checked
fix: step 2: depends names a task id earlier in the sequence

what: prints "<n> findings" on failure but "spec check: 0 findings" on success: two forms of one line
fix: one form: `spec check: <n> findings`

what: kept.after REFERENCES objects(id), but MySQL sets a kept statement's after to a namespace id after a USE (read/mod.rs:247) and after CREATE DATABASE (read/mod.rs:300): every MySQL dump with an account or grant after a USE is refused by the database
evidence: engines/mysql/src/read/mod.rs:240-248, :300; sections.rs Kept.after "The part it comes after"
fix: kept: after_namespace REFERENCES namespaces(id) and after_object REFERENCES objects(id), at most one set (CHECK); t02 step 3/4 map Kept.after to whichever it names

what: step 3: cortex_rows "writes no row of schema"; step 4: cortex_schema takes "engine and version from the row of schema"; step 6: the kit's round trip uses cortex_rows then cortex_schema with no store — no schema row, so the round trip cannot run
fix: cortex_rows(schema, engine, identity) writes the schema row too, from an identity the caller gives (id, name, comment, created_at): the store gives the real one, the kit a fixed one

what: step 4 sets the section's format to engine.format(); the example engine's format() is 1 but its reader leaves the section's format 0 (sections.rs default): Quill's round trip differs, and in general the format a schema was read with is lost
evidence: crates/engine/tests/example/mod.rs:195 fn format → 1; reader never sets section.format
fix: schema/cortex/schema.sql gains section_format INTEGER NOT NULL (the engine storage version its options were written in, as the section holds it); t02 step 3 writes it, step 4 reads it back

what: Schema.format (the model's file format, FORMAT) is not said; only the section's layout and format are
fix: step 4: the schema's format is the model's FORMAT

what: no position: SchemaSection.requires is a list in order, and rules nothing-lost says "every order"
fix: add position INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE; id requirement<n>? keep id the name, add position

what: CHECK (colour GLOB '#rrggbb') is stricter than the model, which accepts any colour text: a schema whose area colour is "teal" or "#ABC" is refused — loss
evidence: crates/model/src/check.rs has no colour rule; schema.rs Area.colour Option<String>
fix: drop the GLOB check; colour TEXT, "as the model holds it"

what: UNIQUE (namespace, kind, name) is weaker than the model, which refuses two objects of one namespace with one name whatever their kinds (check.rs: "another object in its namespace is called")
fix: UNIQUE (namespace, name)

what: UNIQUE (parent, name) does not hold at the top (parent NULL: SQLite treats NULLs as distinct); the model refuses two top namespaces of one name
evidence: check.rs: "another namespace beside it is called"
fix: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX namespaces_name ON namespaces (ifnull(parent, ''), name)

what: the model refuses an object that reads itself and a link with no columns; the cortex allows both
evidence: check.rs: "it reads itself", "it links … no columns"
fix: object_reads CHECK (object <> reads); integrity query link-has-columns

what: TableFile, Migration and Rows are named but their fields and types are not (Migration "of version, name and text"); agent-decides forbids choosing a public item, so the agent cannot build them without a reading
fix: write them: TableFile { name: &'static str, sql: &'static str }; Migration { version: u32, name: &'static str, sql: &'static str }; Rows = BTreeMap<String, Vec<Row>>; Row { table: String, values: BTreeMap<String, Value> }

what: the first part that differs in the kit's round-trip message is not defined (which part, in what form)
fix: the id of the first part, in the schema's order (namespaces, objects with their columns, links, areas, the schema section), whose JSON differs

what: t03 owns a change to tools/check.sh ("cargo clippy and cargo test with --all-features") that the design branch already made
fix: drop tools/check.sh from t03 owns; add it to forbid

what: the samples move to engines/quill/tests/samples with first line quill 2, but their file names (shop.example, machinery.example) are not said: keep or rename to .quill
fix: say: renamed shop.quill and machinery.quill; other.txt kept

what: a flag as the integer 1 or 0 and "read() sets an option only for a column that is not null": linear, columns, subpartition linear, aggregate and key-part desc are NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 columns, and MySQL writes those options only when true (read/table.rs:605,611,625; read/program.rs:347; read/mod.rs:855); read() would set false where the read schema had nothing — the round trip differs
fix: step 2: for a NOT NULL flag column, 1 is the option true and 0 is the option absent; read() sets it only on 1

what: read() rebuilds parts with "empty for a column without a row": MySQL writes JSON null for such a part (read/mod.rs:848), not an empty object
fix: null for a column without a row

what: MySQL's to_key builds columns from column parts only but parts from every part (read/mod.rs:842-861): a key with an expression part has more parts than columns, and key_column_id positions then do not line up with the parts
fix: design session: say whether a key can hold an expression part in MySQL's reader, and if so where its shape goes

what: create writes the schema row and the kinds; import first makes the file by step 4, then writes cortex_rows(imported.schema) — which (after finding 23) holds the schema row and the kinds again: primary keys collide and the import always fails
fix: import does not call create: it makes the file (migrations only) and writes everything, schema row and kinds included, in its one operation

what: create writes the schema row and the kinds outside any operation: "replaying the log rebuilds the model" no longer holds, and "every change belongs to a turn" is broken
fix: drop Store::create from t05 (nothing needs an empty schema before t07); the import's operation writes every row of the file

what: Store::open(folder) names no registry, yet steps 4 and 9 refuse "an engine the registry does not hold" and the tests run on for_tests(): which registry the store holds is not said
fix: Store::open(folder, registry: Registry)

what: Source, ConnectionInfo, TestRecord, StoreError and the arguments of record_test are named but not defined; the turn's who and summary come "as Source gives it"
fix: define them: Source = File { path } or Live { connection, which }, its text `<path>` or `<connection>` (`<connection> (<which joined by ", ">)`); ConnectionInfo { name, engine, values, tested: Option<(at, outcome)> }; record_test(name, outcome: passed|warning|failed, steps: [(step, outcome, said)])

what: the drift check compares PRAGMA table_info (name, type, not null, default, pk): a dropped CHECK, foreign key, UNIQUE or index passes it — "refuses a file whose tables differ" (rules the-schema-decides breach) does not hold
fix: compare each table's and index's sqlite_master sql with the one the shipped files make, exactly

what: one process writes a workspace at a time and "the file's one writer" are stated, never enforced: two processes can write one file and issue interleaved ids
fix: the store holds an exclusive lock on the workspace (a lock file workspace.lock opened exclusively) for as long as it is open, and refuses a second: `the workspace is open in another process`

what: an import writes two databases (the schema file, then workspace.db) with no rule for a failure between them, nor for a file under schemas/ without a row or a row without its file
fix: order and recovery: the file is written first and its workspace row last; Store::open lists a schemas/ file with no row and a row with no file as errors naming each

what: CHECK (length(git_commit) = 40) refuses a commit of a SHA-256 git repository (64 characters)
evidence: git object formats sha1 and sha256
fix: CHECK (length(git_commit) IN (40, 64))

what: the vocabulary guard would flag the merged unit tests of crates/engine/src/live.rs ("host", "port", "user", MySQL field keys), which t03 may not change
fix: t03 owns that tests module and renames the keys to place, door, who

what: the guard over every .rs file would flag crates/model/tests/model.rs ("kind": "view", a MySQL kind id) in a crate t03 may not change
fix: the guard reads src/ only; tests of shared code stay engine-neutral by running on every engine

what: shared words came from schema/cortex only: the store (shared code) uses workspace columns such as connection, which is also a MySQL column (mysql__table_options."connection"); and .count() would match the member rule (count is a MySQL column)
fix: shared words include schema/workspace; a member followed by ( is a call, not a member

what: a file with no row made the whole workspace unopenable, and remove refused a name with no row: no way out
fix: the file restores its own row; a row with no file is an error remove still clears

what: comparing the file's sqlite_master with the table files breaks at the first ALTER TABLE migration (SQLite stores the altered text)
fix: compare with what applying every shipped version to an empty in-memory database makes

what: SchemaInfo's field types and the error for a connection name the check refuses were not given
fix: written out

what: desc is a MySQL column ("desc" of mysql__key_column_options) and a value of the cortex's direction CHECK: the guard would flag merged sections.rs tests (forbidden to t03) and t02's tables.rs, which must write 'desc'
fix: shared words include every value a cortex or workspace CHECK lists

what: ids "after the greatest the file holds": the uuid crate's ContextV7 cannot be seeded; how an id is made greater was the agent's to work out
fix: the store keeps the last id; a not-greater id becomes the last plus one in rand_b, version and variant kept; overflow is an error

what: opened exclusively names no means; an OS lock needs a crate the task does not list
fix: std::fs::File::try_lock (stable in the toolchain, 1.95)

what: an import that fails after making its file leaves a file with no schema row, which the recovery of step 3 cannot restore
fix: a failed import removes its file; on open, a file with no schema row is removed

what: a row with no file is the error did not say whether Store::open fails; if it did, remove could never be reached
fix: open does not fail; schema(name) errors; remove clears the row
